scope: Public source review; source pages retained only in temporary research workspace, no raw golfer dataset acquired

sources.title: What Is Carry in Golf? Trackman Explains the Concept
sources.claim: Carry-flat definition separates carry from finish; not always identical to actual landing on elevated terrain.

sources.title: Map My Bag: Your new golf club selection and practice tool
sources.claim: Maps carry and total separately, rolling average of up to 30 shots per club; suggests six to start.
sources.limitations: Product workflow; no stock percentile or mishit filter specification; 30 cannot establish rare tails.

sources.title: Know your numbers: How Map My Bag can save you strokes
sources.claim: Expert reports golfers often overestimate yardages by 10–15 yd.
sources.limitations: Expert/marketing statement without sample or study method; cannot impose a 10–15 yd correction.

sources.title: Use the Consistency Number for Better Golf Performance
sources.claim: Consistency is standard deviation; one competitive junior example gives carry SD 4.8 yd at 70 yd and 3.5 yd at 80 yd.
sources.limitations: Single student and partial wedge targets; not a full-iron 20-handicap sample; no raw shots/count.

sources.title: New PGA & LPGA Tour Averages | Trackman Insights 2024
sources.claim: Tour means have broad professional sampling and mixed competition/range context.
sources.limitations: Means across golfers are not within-player error distributions; not amateur calibration.

sources.title: Introducing Arccos' New Smart Club Distances – Arccos Golf
sources.claim: Good-strike distance excludes mishits, abnormally long and recovery shots.
sources.limitations: Historical product definition; not whole-shot carry distribution; no filtering thresholds.
sources.pagePublicationOrUpdateDate: Not displayed in extracted article text

sources.title: What is Smart Distance, Smart Range, and Longest? – Arccos Golf
sources.claim: Smart Distance estimates well-struck outcomes with excluded mishits/long/chip/recovery shots; sparse data can be AI-predicted.
sources.limitations: Support page has ambiguous 20+/30-shot wording and variable filters; no exact percentiles.

sources.title: What is Normalized Smart Distances? – Arccos Golf
sources.claim: Distance figures are normalized for environment; users can view/edit included shots.
sources.limitations: Modeled adjusted values are not raw measured flight; no reconstruction algorithm disclosed.

sources.title: How do I included or excluded shots in my Smart Distance? – Arccos Golf
sources.claim: Users may manually include/exclude shots such as duffs and recoveries.
sources.limitations: Inclusion rules can vary by user; selected good-shot results cannot represent every attempted full shot.

sources.title: Understanding Your Club Overview Stats – Arccos Golf
sources.claim: Smart Distance described as a club-dependent percentile of good-contact carry, drivers lower and wedges higher.
sources.limitations: Exact club percentiles and carry measurement/reconstruction method absent; provider claim, not raw data.

sources.title: What Is Distance Distribution? – Arccos Golf
sources.claim: Histogram by club and lie; recommends majority outcome rather than best shot.
sources.limitations: Calls Smart Distance most common carry, unlike percentile description elsewhere; do not equate mode and quantile.

sources.title: What Does the Driving Distance Number Mean? – Arccos Golf
sources.claim: Player driving-distance statistic explicitly P70 carry; par4/par5 tee shots only; recommends 10 tracked rounds.
sources.limitations: Driving statistic only, not every iron Smart Distance; no raw dataset, measured carry method or tail rates.

sources.title: How Do I Read the Dispersion Graph? – Arccos Golf
sources.claim: Ellipse represents approximately 68% of shots; axes use fairway centerline for drives and pin target line for approaches.
sources.limitations: Recorded line is not necessarily intended line; no raw sample or ellipse-fit algorithm; not interchangeable with 80% core.

sources.title: What Is Directional Bias? – Arccos Golf
sources.claim: Bias is club-specific; extreme mishits filtered; fairway/pin reference axes.
sources.limitations: Does not establish universal left-long/right-short correlation or target intent.

sources.title: What is the P-AVG (Performance Average Distance)? – Shot Scope
sources.claim: Performance Average removes long and short outliers; excludes positional shots and shots inside50yd.
sources.limitations: Well-struck distance reference; no carry separation or filtering thresholds in article; not unfiltered error shape.

sources.title: You Don't Have as Much Control over the Golf Ball as You Think · Practical-Golf.com
sources.claim: One near-scratch golfer hit20 shots per club indoors: SW105 target97–117;8i160 target148–171;5i195 target178–201 yd.
sources.limitations: Small good-striking session, perfect mat and no pressure; descriptive min/max, not central intervals or hard bounds; no raw coordinates.
sources.pagePublicationOrUpdateDate: Not displayed in extracted article text

sources.title: The Driver Dispersion Test: How To Make Smarter Decisions Off the Tee · Practical-Golf.com
sources.claim: Single-player30-shot driver exercise separates250yd carry from270–275 total and about68yd lateral width.
sources.limitations: One-player example; width is not SD or universal probability coverage; no shot-level export.
sources.pagePublicationOrUpdateDate: Not displayed in extracted article text

sources.title: How Far Do Golfers Hit Their Irons? Why Approach Play Is so Important · Practical-Golf.com
sources.claim: Aggregate iron distances/GIR/proximity contextualize ability differences.
sources.limitations: Between-player mean distances and short-of-green results do not identify within-club carry error or execution/selection causes.
sources.pagePublicationOrUpdateDate: Not displayed in extracted article text

sources.title: Knowing the actual distances of each of your golf clubs is vital information to have. Find out why in our latest article. · Practical-Golf.com
sources.claim: Instruction explicitly says average carry not best-strike yardage; wind/lie/slope can cause short misses.
sources.limitations: Coaching explanation, not controlled population distribution.
